claim: WW domain is one of the smallest protein-protein interaction domains composed of only ~35 amino acid residues.
source: WW domain, one of the smallest protein-protein interaction domains composed of only ~35 amino acid residues, are widely distributed in many proteins with diverse functions (e.g. a totally of 95 WW domain in 53 proteins in the human proteome).
evidence: This is stated as an established fact in the introduction, drawing from general scientific knowledge about WW domains.

claim: The human proteome contains 95 WW domains in 53 proteins.
source: WW domain, one of the smallest protein-protein interaction domains composed of only ~35 amino acid residues, are widely distributed in many proteins with diverse functions (e.g. a totally of 95 WW domain in 53 proteins in the human proteome).
evidence: This is stated as a factual count of WW domains in the human proteome.

claim: WW domains organize molecular assemblies by binding to short, proline rich peptide motifs each with ~4–6 residues.
source: WW domains organize molecular assemblies by binding to short, proline rich peptide motifs each with ~4–6 residues (Sudol and Hunter, 2000; Salah, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Type I WW domains bind to a consensus 'PPxY' motif with very modest affinities (with Kd in the range of a few to a few tens of µM).
source: The type I WW domains bind to a consensus 'PPxY' motif (where P is proline, x is any amino acid and Y is tyrosine, also known as PY-motif) with very modest affinities (with Kd in the range of a few to a few tens of µM) (Chong et al., 2010; Kato et al., 2002; Kato et al., 2004; Aragón et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: The human proteome contains ~1,500 'PPxY' motifs in >1000 proteins.
source: The human proteome contains ~1,500 'PPxY' motifs in >1000 proteins (Hu et al., 2004; Tapia et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Most of the WW domains in the human proteome belong to type I (52 out of a total of 95).
source: Most of the WW domains in the human proteome belong to the type I (52 out of a total of 95).
evidence: This is stated as a factual count of WW domain types.

claim: YAP WW domains have been reported to bind to PY motifs from LATS, AMOTs, PTPN14, p73, SMAD1, etc.
source: For example, YAP WW domains have been reported to bind to PY motifs from LATS, AMOTs, PTPN14, p73, SMAD1, etc. (Hao et al., 2008; Oka et al., 2008; Zhang et al., 2008; Chan et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2011; Zhao et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2012; Huang et al., 2013; Liu et al., 2013; Strano et al., 2001; Alarcón et al., 2009; Yi et al., 2013; Michaloglou et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: KIBRA WW domains have been reported to bind to PY-motifs from LATS, AMOTs, and PTPN14.
source: KIBRA WW domains have also been reported to bind to PY-motifs from LATS, AMOTs, and PTPN14 (Baumgartner et al., 2010; Genevet et al., 2010; Yu et al., 2010; Knight et al., 2018; Xiao et al., 2011; Hermann et al., 2018; Wang et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: The WW domains of SAV1 can bind to PY motifs of LATS.
source: The WW domains of SAV1 can bind to PY motifs of LATS (Tapon et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: PY motifs of LATS1, AMOT and PTPN14 have been shown to bind to WW domain-containing NEDD family E3 ligases.
source: Additionally, PY motifs of LATS1, AMOT and PTPN14 have also been shown to bind to WW domain-containing NEDD family E3 ligases (Kim and Jho, 2018; Nguyen and Kugler, 2018; Salah, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Whether YAP is in nuclei or in cytoplasm dictates the fate of cell growth and polarity.
source: Since whether YAP is in nuclei or in cytoplasm dictates the fate of cell growth and polarity (Sun and Irvine, 2016; Moya and Halder, 2019; Fulford et al., 2018; Yu et al., 2015a), it is envisaged that at least some of the WW/PY-motif interactions need to be specific.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: KIBRA WW tandem binds to PTPN14 PY12 with a super strong affinity (Kd ~8.2 nM).
source: We found that the KIBRA WW tandem also binds to PTPN14 PY12 with a super strong affinity (Kd ~8.2 nM) (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 1B and C.

claim: KIBRA WW tandem binds to Dendrin PY23 with a super strong affinity (Kd ~2.1 nM).
source: We also included another PY-motif containing protein Dendrin in the study, serving as a reference for super strong target bindings involving WW domains (Kd ~2.1 nM, Figure 1B and D; also see our recent work by Ji et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 1B and D, and cited work.

claim: KIBRA WW1 has a very weak binding to PTPN14 PY12 (Kd ~32 μM).
source: We further showed that KIBRA WW1 had a very weak binding to PTPN14 PY12 (Kd ~32 μM) and KIBRA WW2 had no detectable binding to PTPN14 PY12 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: KIBRA WW2 has no detectable binding to PTPN14 PY12.
source: We further showed that KIBRA WW1 had a very weak binding to PTPN14 PY12 (Kd ~32 μM) and KIBRA WW2 had no detectable binding to PTPN14 PY12 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: The KIBRA WW tandem binds to AMOT PY34 with a high affinity (Kd ~96 nM).
source: Unexpectedly, the KIBRA WW tandem binds to AMOT PY34 with a high affinity (Kd ~96 nM), although the PY3 sequence severely deviates from the canonical WW domain binding PY-motif of 'PPxY'.
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC experimental data.

claim: The KIBRA WW tandem binds to AMOT PY12 with a very weak affinity (Kd ~16.7 μM).
source: It is important to note that the KIBRA WW tandem binds to AMOT PY12, of which both PY1 and PY2 are canonical PY-motifs but are separated by 130 residues, with a very weak affinity (Kd ~16.7 μM) (Figure 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The KIBRA WW tandem binds to LATS1 PY23 with a Kd of ~0.78 μM.
source: We further found that the KIBRA WW tandem binds to LATS1 PY23 with a Kd of ~0.78 μM (Figure 1B), but much more weakly to the canonical PY1 motif (Kd ~78 μM; Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The YAP WW tandem binds to closely spaced PY-motifs of PTPN14, AMOT, and Dendrin with affinities of a few hundred to a few thousand fold weaker than the KIBRA WW tandem does.
source: Very surprisingly, the YAP WW tandem binds to closely spaced PY-motifs of PTPN14, AMOT, and Dendrin with affinities of a few hundred to a few thousand fold weaker than the KIBRA WW tandem does (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The structures of the WW tandems in the KIBRA/PTPN14, KIBRA/AMOT, and KIBRA/LATS1 complexes are extremely similar, with overall pairwise RMSD values in the range of 0.63–1.0 Å.
source: The structures of the WW tandems in the three complexes are extremely similar, with the overall pairwise RMSD values in the range of 0.63–1.0 Å (Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural analysis of crystal structures shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Every WW domain forms a canonical β-sheet fold with three anti-parallel β-strands.
source: Every WW domain forms a canonical β-sheet fold with three anti-parallel β-strands.
evidence: This is stated based on structural analysis of the crystal structures.

claim: The two WW domains align with each other in a head-to-tail manner in the KIBRA WW tandem.
source: The two WW domains align with each other in a head-to-tail manner, so that the two PY-motif binding pockets of the WW tandem are positioned right next to each other to accommodate the two PY-motifs in each of the three targets.
evidence: This is stated based on structural analysis of the crystal structures.

claim: The head-to-tail orientation of the WW tandem imposes a restriction that the target peptide can only bind to the WW tandem in an antiparallel manner (i.e. 1st PY binds to WW2 and 2nd PY binds to WW1).
source: The head-to-tail orientation of the WW tandem imposes a restriction that the target peptide can only bind to the WW tandem in an antiparallel manner (i.e. 1st PY binds to WW2 and 2nd PY binds to WW1; Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated based on structural analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The WW tandem forms a stable structural supramodule by extensive interactions between the inter-domain linker (residues I35-L57) and an α-helix extension (αC) immediately following WW2 via hydrophobic, charge-charge and hydrogen bond interactions.
source: Though the direct contacts between the two WW domains in the tandem are minimal, the WW tandem forms a stable structural supramodule by extensive interactions between the inter-domain linker (residues I35-L57) and an α-helix extension (αC) immediately following WW2 via hydrophobic, charge-charge and hydrogen bond interactions (detailed in Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated based on structural analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Perturbations of the supramodule formation (e.g. single point mutations such as I35D, F47A, L57D, and W88A, or deletion of αC) invariably weakened the binding of the WW tandem to its targets.
source: Perturbations of the supramodule formation (e.g. single point mutations such as I35D, F47A, L57D, and W88A, or deletion of αC) invariably weakened the binding of the WW tandem to its targets (Figure 3B), indicating that formation of the WW12 supramodule is critical for high affinity bindings to the three targets studied here as well as to the PY23 of Dendrin (Ji et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by mutational analysis data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: MAGI2 WW tandem binds to PTPN14 PY12 with a strong affinity (Kd ~55 nM).
source: To our delight, ITC assays showed that MAGI2 and MAGI3 WW tandems indeed bind to PTPN14 PY12 with strong affinities (Kd values of ~55 nM and ~103 nM, respectively, Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: MAGI3 WW tandem binds to PTPN14 PY12 with a strong affinity (Kd ~103 nM).
source: To our delight, ITC assays showed that MAGI2 and MAGI3 WW tandems indeed bind to PTPN14 PY12 with strong affinities (Kd values of ~55 nM and ~103 nM, respectively, Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: MAGI1 WW tandem binds to PTPN14 PY12 with a modest affinity (Kd ~4 μM).
source: Correspondingly, MAGI1 WW tandem was found to bind to PTPN14 PY12 with a modest affinity (Kd ~4 μM; Figure 3D), presumably due to the spatial hindrance caused by the extra amino acids in the linker.
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: MAGI2 WW tandem binds to Dendrin PY23 with an extremely high affinity (Kd ~2.3 nM).
source: We further found that MAGI2 and MAGI3 WW tandems bind to Dendrin PY23 with extremely high affinities (Kd values of ~2.3 and~3.6 nM, Figure 3—figure supplement 2B), further supporting the conclusion that MAGI2, MAGI3 and KIBRA WW tandems share a high similarity in target bindings.
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: MAGI3 WW tandem binds to Dendrin PY23 with an extremely high affinity (Kd ~3.6 nM).
source: We further found that MAGI2 and MAGI3 WW tandems bind to Dendrin PY23 with extremely high affinities (Kd values of ~2.3 and~3.6 nM, Figure 3—figure supplement 2B), further supporting the conclusion that MAGI2, MAGI3 and KIBRA WW tandems share a high similarity in target bindings.
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The overall structures of KIBRA and MAGI2 WW tandems in complexes with ligands are similar to each other (RMSD values of 2.3–2.7 Å for the Cα atoms).
source: A structural comparison of the MAGI2 WW tandem in complex with Dendrin with those of the KIBRA WW tandem in complex with various ligands shown in Figure 2 showed that the overall structures of KIBRA and MAGI2 WW tandems in these complexes are similar to each other (RMSD values of 2.3–2.7 Å for the Cα atoms, Figure 3—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C.

claim: The inter-domain linker of the YAP WW tandem is unstructured and there is no C-terminal helix following YAP WW2.
source: First, the inter-domain linker of the YAP WW tandem is unstructured and there is no C-terminal helix following YAP WW2.
evidence: This is stated based on structural analysis of the YAP WW tandem crystal structures.

claim: The two WW domains of YAP do not form a supramodule due to very limited inter-domain contact.
source: Thus, the two WW domains of YAP do not form a supramodule due to very limited inter-domain contact.
evidence: This is stated based on structural analysis of the YAP WW tandem crystal structures.

claim: The Dendrin PY23 binds to the YAP WW tandem in a parallel orientation (i.e. PY2 binds to WW1 and PY3 binds to WW2).
source: Second, the Dendrin PY23 binds to the YAP WW tandem in a parallel orientation (i.e. PY2 binds to WW1 and PY3 binds to WW2), instead of the antiparallel binding orientation observed for the KIBRA/MAGI2 WW tandems.
evidence: This is stated based on structural analysis of the YAP WW tandem/Dendrin complex structures.

claim: The I35D substitution weakened KIBRA's binding to PTPN14 PY12 by ~50 fold.
source: Indeed, the I35D substitution weakened KIBRA's binding to PTPN14 PY12 by ~50 fold, and the L330D mutation decreased MAGI2's binding to Dendrin PY23 by ~57 fold (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by mutational analysis data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The L330D mutation decreased MAGI2's binding to Dendrin PY23 by ~57 fold.
source: Indeed, the I35D substitution weakened KIBRA's binding to PTPN14 PY12 by ~50 fold, and the L330D mutation decreased MAGI2's binding to Dendrin PY23 by ~57 fold (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by mutational analysis data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The L244D mutation had no impact on YAP's binding to either Dendrin PY23 or AMOT PY12.
source: Totally consistent with the structural finding of very little coupling between the two WW domains in YAP, the L244D mutation had no impact on YAP's binding to either Dendrin PY23 or AMOT PY12 (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by mutational analysis data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Deleting the Gly residue (Gly553) in the three-residue linker of LATS1 PY23 converted the LATS1 mutant ('LATS1-Δ553') into a very strong binder of the KIBRA WW tandem (Kd ~17 nM).
source: Strikingly, deleting the Gly residue (Gly553) in the three-residue linker of LATS1 PY23 converted the LATS1 mutant ('LATS1-Δ553') into a very strong binder of the KIBRA WW tandem (Kd ~17 nM; Figure 4F), indicating that a two-residue linker between the two PY-motifs is optimal for specific and high affinity binding to the KIBRA, MAGI2 and MAGI3 WW tandems.
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Shortening the linker of the PTPN14 PY12 to one residue (R, 1res) weakened its binding to both KIBRA and MAGI3 WW tandems by as much as ~4400 fold.
source: We further showed that shortening the linker of the PTPN14 PY12 to one residue (R, 1res) weakened its binding to both KIBRA and MAGI3 WW tandems by as much as ~4400 fold (Figure 4G; also see Ji et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by mutational analysis data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Lengthening the linker of the PTPN14 PY12 to three residues (RRP, 3res) significantly weakened its bindings to the KIBRA and MAGI3 WW tandems.
source: Similarly, lengthening the linker of the PTPN14 PY12 to three residues (RRP, 3res) also significantly weakened its bindings to the KIBRA and MAGI3 WW tandems (Figure 4G).
evidence: This claim is supported by mutational analysis data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: KIBRA binds to LATS1-Δ553 stronger than to WT LATS1 in co-immunoprecipitation assays with full-length proteins expressed in HEK293A cells.
source: We confirmed that KIBRA indeed binds to LATS1-Δ553 stronger than to WT LATS1 using a co-immunoprecipitation-based assay with the full-length proteins expressed in HEK293A cells (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experimental data shown in Figure 5A and B.

claim: Cells expressing LATS1-Δ553 had diminished YAP and LATS1 phosphorylations when compared with cells expressing WT LATS1 upon treatment with LPA, serum stimulation, LatB, or serum starvation.
source: Upon treatment with lysophosphatidic acid (1 µM LPA), serum stimulation (1% FBS), latrunculin B (LatB, 0.2 mg/ml), or serum starvation (-FBS), which are well-known signals for the Hippo pathway (Yu et al., 2012; Meng et al., 2015), cells expressing LATS1-Δ553 had diminished YAP and LATS1 phosphorylations when compared with cells expressing WT LATS1 (Figure 5C–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot experimental data shown in Figure 5C–F.

claim: Substitution of R440 with Ala weakened PTPN14's binding to KIBRA by 17-fold.
source: For example, R440 of PTPN14 PY12 forms salt bridges with D17 and D19 in the WW1 of the KIBRA WW tandem (Figure 2A). Substitution of R440 with Ala weakened PTPN14's binding to KIBRA by 17-fold (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by mutational analysis data shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: Truncating the C-terminal extension of PTPN14 PY12 weakened its binding to the WW tandems of KIBRA and MAGI3.
source: Truncating this C-terminal extension weakened PTPN14 PY12's binding to the WW tandems of KIBRA and MAGI3 ('Del-C' in Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by mutational analysis data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Converting the non-canonical PY-motifs of PTPN14 PY12 into canonical ones (i.e. 'PPxY') further enhanced its binding to both KIBRA and MAGI3 WW tandems.
source: Third, converting the non-canonical PY-motifs into canonical ones (i.e. 'PPxY') further enhanced PTPN14 PY12's binding to both KIBRA and MAGI3 WW tandems ('2Pro' and '4Pro' in Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by mutational analysis data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: All substitutions of the first Pro of the second PY in the Dendrin PY23 peptide with Leu, Ala, Val, Cys, Ser, Ile, Thr, and Met weakened the peptide's binding to the KIBRA and MAGI3 WW tandems.
source: As expected, all substitutions weakened the peptide's binding to the tandems (Figure 6C,D and E, and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by mutational analysis data shown in Figure 6C, D, E, and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Substitutions of the Pro residue with Cys, Ala, Ser, Thr, and Val lead to only mild weakening of the binding to KIBRA and MAGI3 WW tandems.
source: However, substitutions of the Pro residue with Cys, Ala, Ser, Thr, and Val lead to only mild weakening of the binding, whereas substitutions with bulky hydrophobic Leu, Met and Ile essentially disrupted the binding.
evidence: This claim is supported by mutational analysis data shown in Figure 6C, D, E, and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Substitutions of the Pro residue with bulky hydrophobic Leu, Met and Ile essentially disrupted the binding to KIBRA and MAGI3 WW tandems.
source: However, substitutions of the Pro residue with Cys, Ala, Ser, Thr, and Val lead to only mild weakening of the binding, whereas substitutions with bulky hydrophobic Leu, Met and Ile essentially disrupted the binding.
evidence: This claim is supported by mutational analysis data shown in Figure 6C, D, E, and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: 132 human proteins contain the 'ΦΦxYxxΨPxY' motifs.
source: We searched for proteins in the UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot database (UniProt Consortium, 2019) and identified 132 human proteins containing the 'ΦΦxYxxΨPxY' motifs (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by a database search as indicated in Supplementary file 3.

claim: JCAD binds strongly to the KIBRA WW tandem (Kd ~58 nM).
source: As expected, both JCAD and USP6NL bind strongly to the KIBRA WW tandem (Figure 7C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 7C and D.

claim: USP6NL binds strongly to the KIBRA WW tandem (Kd ~110 nM).
source: As expected, both JCAD and USP6NL bind strongly to the KIBRA WW tandem (Figure 7C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: PTPN21 PY12 binds to KIBRA WW tandem with essentially the same affinity as PTPN14 PY12 (Kd ~8 nM).
source: PTPN21 PY12 and PTPN14 PY12 bind to KIBRA WW tandem with essentially the same affinity (Kd ~8 nM), as the sequences of these two peptides are very similar.
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC experimental data and sequence similarity analysis.

claim: β-Dystroglycan can bind to KIBRA WW tandem with a high affinity (Kd ~96 nM).
source: Interestingly, β-Dystroglycan, a protein known to play critical roles in Hippo signaling-related cell adhesion and cell growth (Morikawa et al., 2017; Gawor and Prószyński, 2018), can also bind to KIBRA WW tandem with a high affinity (Kd ~96 nM, Figure 7E).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: WW tandems can bind to target proteins with extremely high affinity and with very high sequence specificity.
source: In this study, we discovered that WW tandems, but not individual WW domains, can bind to target proteins with extremely high affinity and with very high sequence specificity.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the experimental data presented throughout the study.

claim: Strong bindings of WW tandems are realized by both highly synergistic conformational coupling of two WW domains connected in tandem and two PY-motifs separated by a two and only two amino acid residues linker.
source: Such strong bindings are realized by both highly synergistic conformational coupling of two WW domains connected in tandem and two PY-motifs separated by a two and only two amino acid residues linker.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the structural and biochemical data presented throughout the study.

claim: The tight binding between KIBRA and Dendrin (Kd ~2.1 nM) is critical for KIBRA (and its associated AMPA receptors) localization in neuronal synapses and for synaptic plasticity.
source: For example, we recently showed that the tight binding between KIBRA and Dendrin (Kd ~2.1 nM) is critical for KIBRA (and its associated AMPA receptors) localization in neuronal synapses and for synaptic plasticity (Ji et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The binding of the KIBRA tandem to PTPN14 is ~1,400 fold stronger than the binding of YAP to PTPN14.
source: For example, the bindings of the KIBRA, MAGI2, and MAGI3 tandems to PTPN14 (and PTPN21) are so much stronger than the binding of YAP to PTPN14 (~1,400 fold difference; Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is based on comparison of binding affinity data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The binding of the KIBRA tandem to LATS1 is ~4.5 fold stronger than YAP tandem to LATS1.
source: Similarly, the binding of the KIBRA tandem (or MAGI2 and MAGI3 WW tandems) to LATS1 is ~4.5 fold stronger than YAP tandem to LATS1 (Figure 3D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1F), therefore KIBRA might be able to modulate the concentration of the LATS1/YAP complex formation by competing with YAP for binding to LATS1.
evidence: This claim is based on comparison of binding affinity data shown in Figure 3D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Enhancing the KIBRA/LATS1 binding by deleting Gly553 in the LATS1 PY23 linker can effectively block LATS1-mediated YAP phosphorylation.
source: This is supported by the finding that further enhancing the KIBRA/LATS1 binding by deleting Gly553 in the LATS1 PY23 linker can effectively block LATS1-mediated YAP phosphorylation, presumably due to the effective sequestration of LATS1-Δ553 by KIBRA (Figure 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: A Gly553Glu mutation of LATS1 was found in patients with renal cell carcinoma.
source: Interestingly, a Gly553Glu mutation of LATS1 was found in patients with renal cell carcinoma (Yu et al., 2015b).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: β-Dystroglycan may be a key regulator in cell growth and neuronal synaptic functions via specifically binding to KIBRA.
source: Therefore, β-Dystroglycan may be a key regulator in cell growth and neuronal synaptic functions via specifically binding to KIBRA.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the binding data and known roles of β-Dystroglycan.
